lines.say: {hook}How does the print get onto this box? {q}Flexography! Here's the four-roller machine examiners want you to sketch.
{pan}It starts with an ink pan. {fr}Roller one, the fountain roller, dips in and picks up ink.
{an}It hands the ink to roller two, the anilox roller, covered in tiny cells. {db}A doctor blade scrapes off the extra, {cells}so every cell holds the same amount.
{pc}Roller three is the plate cylinder. {plate}It's wrapped in a flexible photopolymer plate, with the design raised up, like a rubber stamp. {ink}So only the raised bits get inked.
{ic}Roller four, the impression cylinder, presses the board onto the plate. {sm}Slow it right down. {pr}The pressure transfers the ink. {run}Printed!
{vs}So why not use gravure? {a1}Gravure needs a copper cylinder with the image engraved into it. {a1b}Flexo plates are just photopolymer, so setting up is cheaper and quicker.
{a2}That makes it great for shorter runs and quick changes. {a3}And the soft plate squashes onto uneven surfaces, like corrugated board.
{tip}In the exam: sketch all four rollers in order, label them, and say what each one does.
{o}Try this question and more at TrainTanmay. Link in bio!
